title: Best-arm identification with bounded rewards: fixed budget and known difficulty upper bound.
summary: The algorithm knows a hardness upper bound controlling all arm gaps and identifies the best arm under a fixed sample budget. Performance is the maximum identification error over that hardness class. Constants in an error exponent and multiplicative approximation of the probability are different comparisons.

description_paragraphs: The algorithm knows a hardness upper bound controlling all arm gaps and identifies the best arm under a fixed sample budget. Performance is the maximum identification error over that hardness class. Constants in an error exponent and multiplicative approximation of the probability are different comparisons.

model.instance: Arm reward distributions are fixed, unknown, and supported on $[0,1]$, with a unique best arm. The arm count $K$, budget $T$, and bound $h$ are public, and $H(\nu)=\sum_{i\ne b}(\mu_b-\mu_i)^{-2}\le h$. Neither the actual gaps nor $H$ are revealed.

assumptions.description: Each fixed distribution nu_i is supported on [0,1], and every call returns a fresh independent sample.

assumptions.description: The instance satisfies H(ν) = Σ_{i≠b}(μ_b − μ_i)⁻² ≤ h, with unique best arm b. Only the upper bound h is public; the actual gaps are hidden.

model.parameter_domain_description: K: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); h: $h\ge11K^2$ (the currently documented window, public).
interaction_timing: The environment fixes an admissible ν. The learner receives K, T, and h.
At each time $t=1,\ldots,T$, select an arm using past feedback and draw one fresh sample.
Recommend one arm after exactly T calls.

model.adversary_information: The unknown distribution or parameter is fixed before interaction. Learner randomness and sample randomness are independent. No adversary changes the distribution round by round from the learner's history.
unresolved_applicability: Instance-adaptive algorithms with unknown h have a different information specification. This setting does not imply one exact error exponent shared by all instances.
description_paragraphs: Fixed unknown reward distributions $\nu_i$, supported on [0,1], with each sample fresh and independent.
Public $h$ bounds instance complexity through $H\le h$. Individual arm gaps remain hidden.
The recommendation $\widehat b_T$ after exhausting the fixed budget; the native error is misidentification probability.
Assume $K\ge2$, a fixed integer sample budget $N=T\ge1$, and a unique best arm. The recorded comparison requires $h\ge11K^2$; other complexity windows require their own status assessment.
The sum defining $H$ includes suboptimal arms only. The source UCB-E quantity $H_1$ repeats the minimum-gap term for the best arm; this conversion is recorded in the bound's derivation.

description_paragraphs: Sampling an arm with bounded rewards:
An arm is selected before one fresh reward sample is returned.

resource.budget_semantics: Use exactly T arm pulls, then recommend one arm to minimize worst-case error probability.
resource.scalarization: Retain the native objective and complete resource vector. At fixed $T$, compare cumulative regret. Best-arm-identification stopping times and error probabilities use their own task-specific criteria.
resource.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
resource.online_cost: All causal algorithms that know $h$ are permitted. UCB-E is tuned using this public upper bound. Empirical means, index comparisons, and recommendation are internal computations. Exponential-order error comparisons retain polynomial prefactors and their validity windows.
resource.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
resource.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.
description_paragraphs: Use exactly $T$ arm pulls and compare the final error probability $p_{\mathrm{error}}$. This objective does not involve a random stopping time.
All causal algorithms knowing h are allowed. UCB-E is tuned using the public upper bound h.
Sample averages, index comparisons, and recommendation are internal operations. Error-exponent comparisons retain polynomial prefactors and applicability windows.

Information calls, arithmetic, communication rounds, and memory are measured separately. Exact real internal computation is excluded from information complexity unless explicitly charged. This does not imply a bit-complexity bound.

algorithms.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
algorithms.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All causal randomized algorithms using $K,T,h$ are allowed, with exactly $T$ samples. Hidden gaps and true $H$ are inaccessible.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real internal computation is allowed. Policies know h; UCB-E tuning uses that public complexity bound. Sample means, index comparisons, and recommendations are internal work. Error-exponent comparisons retain polynomial prefactors and validity windows; feedback complexity gives no arithmetic or bit bound.
algorithms.parallelism: Interaction proceeds in sequential time rounds. A two-point evaluation is one pair of same-round responses only where explicitly permitted; it is not equivalent to two independent rounds.
description_paragraphs: All measurable causal randomized policies respecting the stated timing are allowed. The private seed is independent of the fixed instance and future samples. Apart from explicit feedback, output, and budget requirements, there are no restrictions on linear spans, iteration form, internal arithmetic, memory, or communication.

conditions: Require $K\ge2$, $h\ge11K^2$, and $T\ge2K$, with instance complexity $H\le h$.
The budgets must additionally satisfy both $T\ge h^2\log(6TK)/900$ and $T\ge144h\log(2TK)$.

bounds.hidden_constants: Universal constants independent of the parameters explicitly tracked in this claim
bounds.derivation: The source complexity $H_1$ duplicates the smallest suboptimal gap at the optimal-arm position, so $H_1\le2H\le2h$. Exploration parameter $\alpha=25(T-K)/(72h)$ meets the source condition $\alpha\le25(T-K)/(36H_1)$. Substituting into the UCB-E error bound and using this region's budget condition gives $-\log p^\star\ge T/(144h)$, where $p^\star$ is minimax error over the class with complexity at most $h$.

evidence.supports: The source supports $p^*(K,T,h)\ge\frac16\exp\left(-\frac{120T}{h}\right)$ and the stated reductions, subject to each atomic claim's model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: Complexity is $H=\sum_{i\ne i^\star}\Delta_i^{-2}$. Over instances with complexity at most $h$, worst-case error is at least $(1/6)\exp(-120T/h)$ when $T\ge h^2\log(6TK)/900$. A separate source result for instance-adaptive policies contains $\log K$ and is not mixed with this class-budget target.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $p^*(K,T,h)\le\min\left\{1,\ 2TK\exp\left(-\frac{T-K}{36h}\right)\right\}$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: UCB-E has error probability at most $2TK\exp(-2\alpha/25)$, provided $\alpha\le25(T-K)/(36H_1)$. In $H_1$, the best-arm coordinate duplicates the inverse squared smallest suboptimality gap.
